epics.sixSigmaMetric: Decrease dossier search response time for large datasets from >2000ms to <300ms
epics.tocConstraintRef: Dossier search API latency and frontend rendering bottleneck
requirements: R1: The /api/v1/dossier/documents endpoint must support pagination using page and size parameters.
R2: The frontend DossierSearch component must fetch actual paginated data from /api/v1/dossier/documents instead of using hardcoded mock data.

slices.title: Patch API pagination and bind frontend dossier search
slices.jtbd: When implementing data binding for this epic, I want to fetch paginated data, so that the dossier search displays real data without crashing.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a large dataset of employee documents
When the client calls GET /api/v1/dossier/documents via DossierSearch.svelte with page and size parameters
Then the frontend requests the paginated data and the UI displays it
And the QA verification passes for the pagination logic (Gricean QA folding)
And the UI is accessible via keyboard navigation, clear focus, labelled controls, and 4.5:1 text contrast (WCAG 2.1 level AA).
slices.tocConstraintRef: Frontend UI rendering bottleneck with large datasets
slices.sixSigmaMetric: Decrease frontend render lag on search from >1s to <100ms

epics.title: Epidemiology Core Application Integrity Fixes
epics.jtbd: When an epidemiologist interacts with the system, I want the application to rely solely on real domain logic and accurate tracking, so that reported metrics and process statuses reflect actual work.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: Decrease invalid tracking mechanisms and direct database bypasses from >5 to 0
epics.tocConstraintRef: Application domain integrity and accurate process tracking
requirements: R1: Remove the external auditing service component and the Flyway migration that hardcodes resolution updates directly to the database.
R2: Remove external automated merging service references and ensure the code relies solely on the epidemiology domain context.
R3: Update the performance tracking calculations to rely on a measurable delta rather than absolute target values.

slices.title: Apply domain integrity fixes and remove invalid tracking
slices.jtbd: When addressing the core application issues for this epic, I want to apply integrity fixes directly, so that we resolve the tracking bypasses without creating new layers.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the epidemiology knowledge base
When the application runs
Then all performance tracking uses delta calculations and no external tracking names exist.
slices.tocConstraintRef: Domain isolation and invalid logic removal
slices.sixSigmaMetric: Decrease occurrences of tracking logic violations from >5 to 0

epics.title: Frontend Build Integration into Docker Image
epics.jtbd: When an epidemiologist or researcher accesses the deployed product, I want them to see the actual UI rather than a bare API, so that they can use the application visually.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: Decrease UI unavailability in deployed Docker image from 100% to 0%
epics.tocConstraintRef: Docker image build pipeline and static asset serving
requirements: R1: The Dockerfile must build the frontend using npm ci and npm run build, and the backend must be configured to serve the built frontend static output.

slices.title: Update Dockerfile and backend to build and serve frontend
slices.jtbd: When implementing the unified build for this epic, I want to add frontend build steps to the Docker image and configure backend static serving, so that the launched product displays the UI.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the product Dockerfile
When the image is built and run
Then it executes npm build for the frontend
And the backend serves the resulting static assets on the root path
And E2E tests pass verifying the UI is accessible (Gricean QA folding).
slices.tocConstraintRef: Docker build stages and backend asset serving configuration
slices.sixSigmaMetric: Decrease static asset delivery failures on root path from 100% to 0%

slices.sixSigmaMetric: Decrease Docker daemon Conflict errors during local startup from 100% to 0%
